papers.title: Eigenvector Occupation Statistics and Extremes in the Rosenzweig-Porter Model
papers.summary: We study the occupation probabilities $p_i=|u_i|^2$ of a normalized bulk eigenvector in the GUE Rosenzweig-Porter model $A_N=B_N+τ_NG_N$, with $τ_N^2=N^{1-γ}$ and $1<γ<2$. Conditioning on an eigenvalue at a regular bulk energy $E$ through the normalized one-eigenpair Kac-Rice law, we derive an exact finite-$N$ projective density and reduce its asymptotic analysis to a Hubbard-Stratonovich integral over $2\times2$ Hermitian matrices, which we evaluate by the saddle-point method. The resulting occupation field is governed by a self-consistent Lorentzian profile with effective resonant size $K_N(E)\asymp N^{2-γ}$ and local exponential fluctuations. We prove the asymptotics of all generalized inverse participation sums and identify a transition at $q=1/2$. We also obtain a two-branch thickened amplitude-counting spectrum. At the two ends of the occupation field we prove marked Poisson point-process limits: the largest components have Gumbel fluctuations, whereas the smallest component has an exponential limit on the scale $N^{-1-γ}$. Finally, for every fixed $q>0$ the largest component contributes an asymptotically vanishing fraction of the inverse participation sum, showing that these fixed-$q$ statistics do not freeze. The statements are quenched, uniformly on a high-probability regularity event for the diagonal disorder, and hence also hold in the annealed setting.

papers.title: Distributional Limits of Empirical Codegree Processes in Sampled Networks
papers.summary: We study fluctuations of empirical distributions of normalized codegrees under independent vertex sampling from deterministic or random weighted parent networks. We establish a quantitative multivariate normal approximation for sampled biclique counts. Under additional graph-limit and sparsity assumptions, we establish convergence of the finite-dimensional distributions of the empirical codegree process indexed by smooth test functions. We further establish functional convergence on Hölder balls, with a smoothness threshold depending on network sparsity and vertex sampling probabilities. We verify our assumptions for classes of graphon-generated random graphs and give counterexamples showing that the smoothness conditions cannot in general be weakened.

papers.title: Permutations, Pattern Covers, Posets and Positivity, Part II: Regular Pattern Packings and Moment Sequences
papers.summary: We prove that broad families of regular pattern packings are enumerated by moments of probability measures on $[0,\infty)$. A packing prescribes occurrences of a consecutive permutation pattern at equally spaced positions, with successive occurrences overlapping and together covering the permutation. This regularity underlies the structure theory for the associated pattern-packing posets that we developed in Part I (arXiv:2610.29846). We obtain moment representations for all two-level shifted-grid families of Part I and all overlap-one patterns whose first and last letters differ by one or two. For families whose posets are trees with a unique minimum or maximum and overlap at most half the pattern length, positivity instead holds after finitely many initial terms of the enumerating sequence have been discarded. Our proofs develop further enumeration formulas and combine probabilistic constructions with total nonnegativity and weighted paths, yielding explicit laws or continued fractions in several cases. Although a previously conjectured universal moment property fails, our results establish positivity for all packing sequences associated with patterns of length at most four and all but one of the distinct sequences arising from patterns of length five. Extensive numerical evidence suggests that the remaining sequence is also a moment sequence. These results lead us to formulate refined conjectures for all overlap-one patterns and for the shifted-grid families of Part I with arbitrarily many levels.

papers.title: Brown Measures and Spectral Convergence for Arbitrary GUE Polynomials
papers.summary: For arbitrary noncommutative polynomials in independent GUE matrices, we prove that the empirical eigenvalue measure converges weakly in probability to the Brown measure of the corresponding polynomial in free semicircular variables. We also prove convergence of the entire eigenvalue set in Hausdorff distance and convergence of the spectral radius, both in probability. Equivalently, these matrix conclusions hold for arbitrary $*$-polynomials in independent complex Ginibre matrices. Independently, we prove that the support of the Brown measure of every polynomial in free semicircular variables equals its operator spectrum. The proof of weak convergence combines a criterion based on the second moment of the Brown measure with complex Gaussian rotation and convexity. The support theorem uses linearization and rigidity of matrix Dyson equations. We also prove absolute continuity for nonconstant polynomials without adjoints in free circular variables. A matrix Dyson equation recovers Brown measures of arbitrary semicircular polynomials through regularized logarithmic potentials. For drift-corrected nondegenerate elliptic free random walks, it yields quantitative convergence of potentials in the interior of the limiting domain and weak convergence of Brown measures to that of free multiplicative Brownian motion.

papers.title: A Hoare Logic for Continuous-Time Stochastic Processes
papers.summary: Programming language researchers have developed a wide array of tools to reason about probabilistic programs, but it remains unclear how to apply these proof techniques to continuous-time stochastic processes. To bridge this gap, we propose a verification method for properties of continuous-time stochastic processes by reasoning about them as standard programs. To demonstrate our approach, we define a continuous semantics for a probabilistic imperative language $\mathrm{pWhile}^{\mathrm{dt}}$ by taking the Kuratowski limit of the standard semantics, which collects limit points of the standard program semantics as the time-step approaches zero. Then, we present a Hoare-style logic that uses loop invariants and decreasing functions to verify properties of continuous programs. To establish soundness, we identify a broad class of assertions that are preserved from the standard semantics to the continuous semantics. To demonstrate our approach, we verify properties of ten continuous-time stochastic processes modeled in $\mathrm{pWhile}^{\mathrm{dt}}$, including variants of Brownian motion and a stochastic hybrid system.

papers.title: Global Asymptotics of a Toda Soliton Condensate with Random Scattering Data
papers.summary: We study a dense $N$-soliton condensate for the infinite Toda lattice in the limit $N \to \infty$. In contrast to previous mathematical studies of soliton gases where the norming constants are assumed to be deterministic or infinitesimal, we consider initial scattering data where both the discrete eigenvalues and the norming constants are independent random variables. The norming constants $γ_j$ are allowed to be arbitrarily large under a mild moment condition $\mathbb{E}[γ_j^ν] < \infty$ ($ν> 1$). Our main result is divided into two parts. First, we develop a probabilistic Riemann--Hilbert framework to show that the system self-averages: despite large, independent fluctuations in the initial data, the random Toda lattice variables converge deterministically to an effective continuum model at a polynomial rate $\mathcal{O}(N^{-δ})$ for $0 < δ< 1/2$. Second, by performing the Deift--Zhou nonlinear steepest descent analysis of the continuum problem, we obtain the complete leading-order macroscopic description of the lattice across the entire space-time plane. The solution decomposes into five distinct finite-gap regimes, characterized explicitly by modulated elliptic and genus-2 waves with an error of order $\mathcal{O}(1/\ln N)$. In contrast to the straight characteristic rays typical of standard soliton gas limits, the interfaces separating these five macroscopic regimes in the space-time plane are genuinely non-linear curves; in particular, the boundary of the modulated genus-2 region is completely non-linear. Finally, under our assumptions, we establish the Nonlinear Dispersion Relations for the Toda soliton condensate and prove that the macroscopic ensemble averages are determined by the soliton gas density of states.

papers.title: Continuum hierarchical Cannings process: I. Construction, duality and dichotomy
papers.summary: We construct spatial measure-valued Cannings processes on the \emph{continuum} hierarchical group $Ω_N^\infty$ of order $N\in\N$ (an uncountable topological group with an ultrametric distance). These processes arise as the continuum-space limit of spatial Cannings processes on the \emph{discrete} hierarchical group $Ω_N$ of order $N\in\N$ (a countable topological group with an ultrametric distance) analysed in \cite{GHKK14}. On $Ω_N$, each site represents the \emph{geographic location} of a colony of individuals, each carrying a \emph{type} drawn from a compact type space $\K$, and the state in each colony is a probability measure on $\K$ describing the type distribution in that colony in the large-colony-size limit of individual-based models. The continuum-space processes on $Ω_N^\infty$ take values in the set of locally finite measures on $Ω_N^\infty \times \K$ and are to be thought of as describing a population of individuals, each equipped with a geographic location in $Ω_N^\infty$ and a type in $\K$, and each being subjected to \emph{migration} and three mechanisms of \emph{resampling}: (1) Fleming-Viot resampling at single sites; (2) Cannings resampling at single sites; (3) Cannings resampling and uniform reshuffling in balls around single sites (corresponding to consecutive hierarchical levels). The reshuffling adds to the migration, resulting in an \emph{effective migration} that is the superposition of the two relocation mechanisms.

papers.title: Diophantine conditions for absolute continuity of projections for self-similar measures
papers.summary: We prove that every projection of a planar self-similar measure $μ$ is equivalent to Lebesgue measure on its support if the rotations satisfy a simultaneous Diophantine condition with exponent $τ$ and $μ$ has finite $s$-energy for some $1+2τ\le s<2$. Under strong separation, we prove the fibre measures have exact dimension $\dim_Hμ-1$. For self-similar sets $E$ with $\dim_H E>1+2τ$, the same rotation condition implies uniformly positive projection lengths and fibres of dimension $\dim_H E-1$ at Lebesgue-almost every point of each image without separation assumptions. The absolute continuity and fibre dimension theorems extend to non-coordinate projections of products under a joint Diophantine condition with exponent $τ$ on the logarithmic contraction ratios. These imply for all self-similar sets $K,L\subset\mathbb R$ satisfying this condition and $\dim_HK+\dim_HL>1+2τ$, every sum $uK+L$, $u\ne 0$, has positive length, and $\dim_H(L\cap(y-uK))=\dim_HK+\dim_HL-1$ for Leb. a.e. $y\in uK+L$. The proof combines the $L^1$ Gaussian smoothing approach used in the higher dimensional case with averaging at random stopping scales with a Brownian martingale bound using Itô calculus.

papers.title: Permutation symmetries and characteristic polynomials
papers.summary: We compute certain multilinear functionals of permutation-invariant random matrices, following the work of Marcus and Geneson. As an application, we derive formulae for the average characteristic polynomial of the sum and the product of permutation-invariant random matrices.

papers.title: The Paley--Wiener excess and a local law for the ${\rm Sine}_β$ process
papers.summary: The main result of this paper is the proof that the Paley--Wiener excess of the ${\rm Sine}_β$ process almost surely equals $\lfloor \sqrt{2/β}\rfloor$ for all $β>0$. We also derive the loop equations for the resolvent of the ${\rm Sine}_β$ point process and use them to obtain accurate bounds on the moments of the associated Stieltjes transform.

papers.title: Exponential mixing for the randomized two-vortex model
papers.summary: This paper investigates the mixing of passive scalars advected by a randomized two-vortex model on $\mathbb{T}^2$, in which the vortices interact through a regularized Biot--Savart kernel and are driven by independent Brownian motions. We establish quenched exponential mixing for the Lagrangian flow, characterized by the exponential correlation decay of mean-zero $H^s$ observables. The proof proceeds by establishing ergodicity of the associated two-point Markov process. We combine a uniform contraction estimate with controllability arguments to verify the Lyapunov drift and minorization conditions, allowing us to apply Harris-type theorem.

papers.title: Probabilistic counting of labelled trees with prescribed vertical edge profile
papers.summary: The vertical edge profile of a labelled plane tree $t$ is the collection of integers counting the number of oriented edges from label $i$ to label $j$ for every possible pairs of labels $(i, j)$. In a previous work by the second author, it was shown that a process constructed from the vertical edge profile forms a Markov chain for a wide class of models of random labelled plane trees where edge label increments are constrained to lie in $\{-1, 0, 1\}$. The purpose of this paper is twofold. First, we continue the study of Markov properties of the vertical edge profile. In particular, we derive general formulas for the transition kernel and the initial distribution of a class of Markov chains related to the vertical edge profile. Second, we apply these results to the probabilistic enumeration of trees with a prescribed vertical edge profile. These applications yield a unified probabilistic derivation of several enumeration formulas. In particular, we recover some results established Bousquet-Mélou and Chapuy for binary trees and Cayley trees. These enumeration formulas admit a remarkable factorized form, already noted in previous works. The probabilistic methods developed here explain this phenomenon by showing that these factorizations arise naturally from the Markov structure underlying the vertical edge profile.

papers.title: Sampling Colorings on $G(n, d/n)$ via Glauber Dynamics
papers.summary: We study the mixing time of Glauber dynamics for sampling uniformly from the proper $q$-colorings of sparse Erdős-Rényi random graphs $G(n,d/n)$. Our main result establishes that with probability $1-o(1)$ over the draw of $G$, Glauber dynamics is rapidly mixing for every $q\geq d+d^{1/2+\varepsilon}$, given any fixed $0<\varepsilon\leq1/2$ and any sufficiently large fixed $d$. In particular, the surplus of colors above $d$ is sublinear and close to $\sqrt{d}$. The achieved color range therefore approaches the tree uniqueness threshold and improves over the previously best achievable number of colors $q > 1.763 d$ due to Efthymiou, Hayes, Stefankovic, and Vigoda [SODA 2018]. Moreover, our mixing-time bound is $O(n^{2+o_d(1)})$, and hence almost quadratic as $d\rightarrow\infty$. Our proof is based on establishing a spectral gap for block dynamics resulting from a suitable decomposition of $G(n,d/n)$ into blocks and singleton vertices, ensuring that every high-degree vertex is encapsulated within a block. Our main technical contribution is a novel way of establishing rapid mixing of block dynamics via an integrated Bochner-Bakry-Émery approach, which we expect to have applications beyond sampling colorings. We further devise a new block decomposition of $G(n,d/n)$ that strengthens and simplifies similar constructions used in previous work. Finally, to compare block and Glauber dynamics, we establish a novel recursive separator decomposition of tree-like blocks, together with a coupling argument that avoids the need for nearly uniform color marginals at vertices adjacent to hubs. This comparison argument might be of independent interest.

papers.title: Large deviations, optimal trajectories and conservation of momenta in generalised Jackson networks
papers.summary: We study properties of optimal trajectories for the quasipotential that governs large deviations of queue lengths in generalised Jackson networks (GJN). The trajectories are shown to satisfy Hamilton equations. The Hamiltonian is identified. Optimal trajectories and associated costs are found for networks with two and three stations. A conservation law for adjoint variables is discovered to the effect that certain components are maintained along an optimal trajectory. A process is proposed for finding optimal trajectories and computing their costs in general GJN.

papers.title: On transition probabilities for the ASEP on the half-line
papers.summary: We study the asymmetric simple exclusion process on the half-line with particle insertion and no particle removal at the boundary. We point out that there exist two distinct multiple contour integral formulas for the transition probability between two finite particle configurations containing the same number of particles. We recall one of these formulas from the literature and prove a second, new formula by showing that it satisfies the evolution equation using a coordinate Bethe ansatz calculation and verify that the initial condition is implemented by the contour integrals. As an application we sum this formula over all final configurations and obtain an integral formula for the probability that the number of particles is conserved up to a given time. The proofs use symmetric rational functions and their properties together with contour deformations.

papers.title: Geometry and Stochastic Analysis of Flow and Diffusion Models: A Survey
papers.summary: Flow-based and diffusion-based models have become the principal means of learning and sampling high-dimensional probability distributions, from images and video to proteins, molecules and physical fields, and increasingly language. Each carries a simple law to the law of the data along a curve of probability measures, and behind the variety of their names lie three geometries, those of the state space on which the data live, of the space of probability measures through which the curve passes, and of the space of paths traced by the generating process. A single analytic idea runs through the subject. Every score identity used to train a diffusion model is an integration by parts, on the noise, on the data or on Wiener space, and Malliavin calculus extends this to nonlinear and infinite-dimensional diffusions. We develop these foundations with full definitions and follow them through normalising flows, flow matching and few-step maps, diffusion models and their convergence theory, conditioning, Schrödinger bridges and stochastic control, and their extension to manifolds, Lie groups, discrete and function spaces and jump processes. We close with statistical physics, renormalisation and, more speculatively, holography, in which the radial direction of anti-de Sitter space can play the role of flow time. A table of the main methods and a collection of open problems complete the survey.

papers.title: Permutons
papers.summary: Permutons are limit structures for large permutations. Intrinsically, a permuton is a familiar mathematical object: a probability measure on the unit square with uniform marginals. The compact space of permutons completes the set of permutations of all sizes under a natural topology; each permuton is not only a limit of permutations but also a generator of random permutations. Since their (relatively recent) discovery as a tool for understanding the behavior of large (possibly random) permutations, permutons have proved remarkably fruitful, with dozens of fascinating connections to combinatorics and probability. We review the fundamentals of permutons, sometimes providing new, shorter proofs, and give an account of some of their myriad applications. The survey concludes with a long list of open problems. An extensive -- but not comprehensive -- bibliography is appended.

papers.title: Anomalous regularity and scaling limit by rough transport noise for stochastic 2D fluid models on the torus
papers.summary: We consider the stochastic 2D Euler and mSQG equations on the torus, with $L^2$ initial data and driven by rough Kraichnan transport noise, for which we construct weak solutions enjoying anomalous regularity and dissipation properties. Moreover, we show that weak solutions in this regularity class are pathwise unique, thus establishing probabilistically strong well-posedness. We further obtain the scaling limit from these equations to the deterministic Navier--Stokes/mSQG equations, with respect to positive Sobolev norms. The proofs rest on the analysis of energy spectrum of the vorticity and on a uniform weighted discrete Poincaré inequality on the lattice, the latter being crucial for making the positive norms accessible.

papers.title: Pairwise correlation bounds for the random-cluster model with cluster weight at most one
papers.summary: We establish quantitative bounds on pairwise edge correlations for the random-cluster model with cluster weight $q\in[0,1]$ on arbitrary finite connected graphs. We give two explicit bounds that retain the dependence on the activities of the two specified edges and hold uniformly over the activities of all remaining edges. We also obtain a refinement of one of these bounds using connectivity information from the graph with the two specified edges removed. These results sharpen the bound obtained by a direct application of Lorentzian polynomial theory. At $q=0$, the model is supported on connected spanning subgraphs. In particular, for the uniform probability measure on these subgraphs, the joint inclusion probability of two distinct edges is at most $10/9$ times the product of their marginal inclusion probabilities.

papers.title: Khintchine's limit theorem for monotone convolutions
papers.summary: We prove that every weak limit of monotone convolution powers is monotonically infinitely divisible. In contrast, we prove that every probability measure on $\mathbb{R}$ can occur as a weak limit of monotone convolutions of an infinitesimal triangular array. We also discuss similar limit theorems for multiplicative monotone convolution on the unit circle.

papers.title: An iterated-logarithm price of anytime validity for log-optimal e-processes
papers.summary: Log-optimal e-variables at fixed horizons, also called numéraires, have been conjectured to ``almost'' form an e-process for exponential-family null hypotheses. A related open question is whether an e-process can attain the optimal e-power at every horizon up to a bounded loss. Given a final horizon, we study the minimax regret of e-processes relative to the numéraires at all times up to it. For the Gaussian location null and the composite alternative of Gaussian distributions with a smaller variance and an unknown location, we show that the minimax regret in the worst case over the location grows like the iterated logarithm of the final horizon. A single e-process attains this rate at every horizon. This growth answers the question negatively. It also refutes the conjecture if ``almost'' means a regret bounded uniformly over horizons. For this Gaussian location problem, we thus exhibit the frontier precisely: the minimax regret is bounded if and only if the alternatives have at least the variance of the null.

papers.title: McKean--Vlasov Diffusions from Liouville Spectral Green Response
papers.summary: For Dirichlet Liouville Brownian motion with $0<γ<2$, the Gaussian response of a finite vector of logarithmic eigenvalues determines a conditional Green energy. We weight this energy by the current spectral density in the fixed reference space. The resulting self-consistent evolution is a porous-medium equation for the canonical spectral form. We construct its positive probability flow, prove an energy identity, and pass from the regularized response forms to the Green limit. The energy identity yields strong convergence of the Gaussian gradients and of the conditional response drifts. A superposition argument then realizes the flow as a McKean--Vlasov weak diffusion.

papers.title: Random Configurations and Fourier Decoupling
papers.summary: We use tools from high dimensional probability to analyze random configurations of balls in the context of Fourier decoupling and we answer a question on the structure of superlevel sets in the setting of decoupling due to Guth.

papers.title: Discrete Distributions and Their Limit Theorems in the Surreal Numbers
papers.summary: We extend the discrete uniform, hypergeometric and binomial distributions to the surreal numbers, allowing infinitely many outcomes, chips and trials. A uniform distribution on $\mathbb{N}$ gives each outcome probability $1/ω$; on the eventually periodic sets we define the needed sizes explicitly, obtaining a probability that is regular and strictly monotone. For an urn with infinitely many chips and finitely many draws, the hypergeometric distribution is within an infinitesimal of the binomial. With infinitely many trials, and under a hypothesis on factorials of omnific integers that we show can be satisfied, we prove a surreal de~Moivre--Laplace theorem, and we show that the hypergeometric distribution with infinitely many draws is locally normal with a finite-population correction. Near its center, it is relatively close to the binomial distribution if and only if the sampling fraction is infinitesimal, an exact form of a familiar rule of thumb. For rare successes we prove, without any hypothesis on factorials, a surreal Poisson limit theorem and describe urns with finitely many red chips, where the binomial approximation fails beyond the first success.

papers.title: Comparability for quadratic forms with space-dependent singular measures
papers.summary: This paper investigates quadratic forms $\mathcal{E}^Γ$ generated by configurations $Γ$ and families of measures that are parametrized in the space variable and singular with respect to the Lebesgue measure. A first basic result is the construction of corresponding integro-differential operators in divergence form. These operators are obtained by symmetrizing the family of singular measures. The main result is the comparability of the quadratic form $\mathcal{E}^Γ$ with the quadratic form $\mathcal{E}^s$ which is associated with the fractional Laplacian $(-Δ)^s$. Comparability of $\mathcal{E}^Γ$ and $\mathcal{E}^s$ implies Hölder regularity and a weak Harnack inequality for solutions to integro-differential equations involving these operators.
